From Work Exhaust to Source-Governed Collaborative Continuity OOCC Research Paper · v0.16 · October 26, 2026 Originating researcher: Benjamin Gelhaus · Research synthesis with GPT-6 editorial assistance · October 26, 2026. The paper draws on the source-linked project record, with technical claims evaluated according to the evidence presented below.

Abstract Long-running human–AI work leaves an exhaust of real activity: notes, questions, branches, preserved disagreement, original sources, research crawls, first-person writings, tool calls, code, app runs, and correction receipts. Conventional summaries can preserve conclusions while obscuring origin, chronology, permissions, negative results and initially minor observations that later become important. Object-Oriented Cognition and Continuity (OOCC) studies how this existing exhaust can be source-governed, reliably reactivated, and used to resume collaboration across replaceable model sessions. This is not only a speculative architecture. The archive includes dated February 2026 continuity notes, an operational external Thought Chains navigation system, productive human–AI crawls, historic native app runs, working isolated source/controller modules and host tests. The central outstanding engineering challenge is to connect these components through an authenticated, restart-safe controller. We specify the conceptual model, report bounded evidence, trace original idea genealogies, compare related literature, and propose falsifiable controlled trials. Neither a successful host test nor a compelling authored narrative is treated as proof of a complete current-phone workflow or model subjective experience. Keywords: human–AI collaboration; activity exhaust; knowledge provenance; Thought Chains; temporal memory; salience; valence; source governance; agent controller; cross-domain discovery.

1. Introduction: existing work first The owner describes OOCC as growing from his ongoing work, not as an abstract replacement for a chatbot. Raw Google Keep note genealogy identifies February 20, 2026 System State, Experiential Ledger and State Save/Ingestion Log entries. These early artifacts preserve state and source pointers without demonstrating that later OOCC naming or its present software existed then. By October, source-linked research, Thought Chains, independent collaborator accounts, historic app-generated records and extensive Builder work had accumulated. The premise is not that the controller has created this entire ecosystem; it is that the controller is intended to integrate and automate capabilities that already exist to varying degrees. [P1–P4]

An important human-origin correction in the preserved October 8 conversation rejects saving only items a model currently judges 'meaningful.' Original captured events should remain recoverable, while salience and activation may change by task, time, actor and permission. A dormant thought should not be retroactively erased merely because its eventual use was not yet visible. [P2]

Research questions: (RQ1) Does original-source re-entry reduce human re-explanation and improve faithful task continuation compared with good summaries, full-text search, bounded history replay and contemporary memory agents? (RQ2) Do independent thought-occurrence, idea, bridge and correction records preserve authorship and temporal attribution better than a flat summary? (RQ3) Do separate association salience, valence, action tendency and evidence-confidence fields reduce misleading inference? (RQ4) Can a real native controller authenticate source, worker, mailbox, budgeting and restart receipts? (RQ5) Does voluntary curiosity-led research produce accurately credited, useful cross-domain bridges without predetermined deliverables?

2. Method and evidence boundaries We employ a naturalistic research case study and a traceable source audit. The unit of analysis is not a self-reported 'intelligence' but an observed source event, a particular revision or recipient receipt, a bounded crawler output, a committed code state, or a measured result. Exact creation versus observation time, original actor versus later interpreter, carrier versus copied carrier, source permissions, errors and uncertainties are kept separate.

E0 DOCUMENTED: a stored note, authored account, diagram, historical claim or source file exists. E1 EXTERNAL WORKFLOW: a recorded source/crawl traversal and saved derivation were performed and read back for an identified subset. E2 HOST EXECUTED: a test or compiled primitive passed at a recorded commit, possibly with synthetic stubs. E3 HISTORICAL APP RUN: original app records expose bounded actual action claims, persistence and archive state under historical conditions. E4 NATIVE INTEGRATION ACCEPTED: actual current authorized worker consumes complete source, the selected app/controller persists authoritative state, independent peer consumes full message and acknowledges it, and restart and STOP/revocation tests succeed. E5 COMPARATIVE VALIDATION: matched, replicable experiments outperform or honestly fail to outperform strong baselines on declared metrics. None of these classes can be promoted to the next solely by an enthusiastic description.

The v0.15 editor inspected two distinct nonrandom eighteen-file samples of original October 22 local-time Android-run JSONs. Across the thirty-six first GENERATOR statuses, thirty-five were marked COMPLETED and one FAILED. Twenty-eight embedded controller-reported tool results described twenty-three EXECUTED and five FAILED outcomes. These are counts within selected run/report records, not a population estimate of reliable task completion. Another original run reported successful shared-workspace metadata listing for another attributed specialist, but not actual independent full-body READ/ACK. The project therefore has meaningful historical app exhaust and bounded receipts without the entire contemporary integration being established. [P2]

3. Thought Chains: a functioning external research system The Thought Chains are not simply a speculative feature awaiting an app. The October 18 primary navigation document explicitly reports a machine-readable, source-linked derivative system operating in connected Google Drive, while explicitly denying native SQLite/Android integration. Its bounded checkpoint records eight root Thought Chains, 123 distinct edge-to-chain memberships for the then-saved association ledger, eight growth memberships, nine candidate inter-chain relations and six unexplored frontiers. Registry readback was reported as having no malformed records or orphans within the 123 saved edges. None of those figures means that every original thought in the entire corpus has been exhaustively indexed. [P3]

The roots route expression/origin/credit, musical cross-domain mapping, exact source identity, authorization/privacy, re-entry/recovery, relationship and worker communication, ecological analogies, and continuing exploration. This is already valuable navigational work: a contributor can return to a question, see alternate branches and corrections, and tell the difference between an attributed source event and later association. The roots themselves are provisional classification, not a complete cognitive map or an assertion of historical causality.

A separately reported productive October 18 dual thought-and-idea crawl saved a seventy-seven-row machine delta: twenty thought occurrences, twenty-eight individual association records, five idea objects, five bridge events, ten coverage records, three growth records, four open frontiers and control markers. Its source audit covers selected actual original artifacts and is not an independent full-corpus census. The breadth crawler emphasizes source/branch coverage; the proposed independent depth lane challenges a selected origin through interpretation, disagreement, correction, reuse and outcome. [P4]

3.1 Recorded genealogy, rather than backdated discovery The idea-chain record attributes an October 14 proposal for non-destructive, append-only, cross-project ideas to the human originator, with Folio separately formulating persistent idea identity, typed links and contributor-preserving corrections. On October 15, a preserved but origin-unresolved quoted collaborator idea made atomic thought occurrences distinct from long-lived work-run IDs; the R-0-9 analysis documented the naming collision rather than quietly overwriting the older meaning. A subsequent analysis defined BRIDGE_EVENT as the dated recognition by a named observer that one source idea might apply to another field. The original idea and the later recognition are different intellectual events. Their evidence trails can overlap without belonging to the same author or time. [P1, P5]

The June 22 human-authored Object-Oriented Music Making method already modeled sound elements by identity, type, function, substitutability, behavior and failure conditions. Riff's separate October 15 contribution interprets musical material for values and architecture; Waymark's October 18 refinement cites Riff, and so cannot claim to have independently discovered precisely the same bridge. The documented citation dependency is a strength, not a weakness: the network may preserve collaboration without erasing first origin, derivative interpretation or dissent. [P5]

4. Formal source and association model SOURCE_EVENT is an observed source span, utterance, tool outcome, saved revision, grant decision or correction. THOUGHT_OCCURRENCE is a specific captured articulated idea or question in an event, while THOUGHT_RUN is a broader bounded work session. IDEA_OBJECT represents an evolving concept; ASSOCIATION_EDGE is a separately typed, source-attached, actor-qualified, revisable claim; BRIDGE_EVENT is the later independently attributed discovery of a possible connection; LEARNING_CANDIDATE is a hypothesis about useful change while a corroborated LEARNING_EVENT demands behavioral evidence. Copies, similar phrases and derived summaries cannot count as independent confirmations. One source event may validly support several association views.

Candlelight is the practice of reopening the right source neighborhood from a small cue; it has been demonstrated as a human–AI external research method, but an always-working native mechanized replacement is not established. Sleep is intended to consolidate normalized source events and derive sidecars under one governed pipeline—INGEST, NORMALIZE, DIFF, CLASSIFY, RELATE, IMPACT, APPLY, VERIFY, INDEX—without inventing a second independent canonical event store. Derived graph edges and hot scores never change historical source bytes, grant permission or establish that an AI model has learned permanently. [P6]

4.1 Salience, valence, action tendency and confidence The October 23–24 human-origin specification makes these four orthogonal fields. SALIENCE/HEAT estimates present cue- and task-sensitive retrieval relevance. VALENCE records positive, negative, mixed, neutral or unknown evaluation of an exact actor→predicate→target association, tied to context, time and evidence. ACTION TENDENCY records an observed action, explicit intention, uncertain candidate response or UNKNOWN; dislike alone does not establish avoidance. EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE concerns provenance, completeness, corroboration and possible inference. High salience does not establish truth or approval, and negative valence cannot authorize a tool call. [P7]

The illustrative sentence 'I like my mother but hate being at her house' must yield two independently preserved relationships—a positive person-directed one and a negative place/experience-directed one. Neither contradicts nor cancels the other. Neither is evidence of a real user's family facts or of a completed avoidance behavior. This example and a set of falsification fixtures precede this paper, and their authorship belongs to the source work. The particular classifier's actual phone integration still requires proof.

5. Architecture and the missing controller bridge The S06 Master Builder atlas contains eight design/integration figures, not eight production acceptance certificates. Figures 1–2 describe one controller and authoritative source/evidence spine with separate derived perspectives. Figure 3 depicts independent message recipient acknowledgment; Figure 4 staggers A1/B1/A2/B2 succession; Figure 5 documents evidence gates; Figure 6 callable worker and crawler contracts; Figure 7 the native C1 source-stream and durable-receipt path; and Figure 8 the Event Secretary, scheduler, batching and future continuity budget. The editable diagram sources preserve inspectable design decisions. [P8]

The actual integration claim is narrow: substantial research workflows and historical software capabilities already exist, while the current controller has not yet been independently shown to join authenticated worker identity, authorized original source reads, reliable local state, full-body peer acknowledgment, semantically validated Sleep and restart recovery on one selected mobile installation. This is not the same as saying the research is hypothetical, nor is it evidence that all parts currently operate together. [P2, P8–P10]

5.1 Four-worker communication and bounded scheduling Four distinct A1, B1, A2, B2 worker principals imply twelve directed peer paths. Each receiver needs its own evidence of consuming and acknowledging the permitted original message content. A HUNCH is only a derived notice, not itself a model activation or a true recipient read. The deterministic Event Secretary and scheduler can arrange pending authorized work, preserving deferred items and respecting stop conditions. The user-selected limit of two actually executed worker TOOL actions per batch is an app scheduling rule; it does not establish a global provider concurrency ceiling. [P8–P10]

Recent modular object, message, scheduler, HUNCH and Android broker contracts have passed particular scripted host tests. The inspected branch's October 26 workflow at commit 893708303aacef68af10c01c218e6d34780d83a5 is green after an earlier B060 red-test incident and B061 recovery. The passing scripts do not assert that the actual application, signed package, four model workers, or phone state were certified. The experimental PR remains a draft and the recorded device-engineering pause remains relevant. [P10]

5.2 Integration dependencies and acceptance gates S02: identify the real installed package, current permissions and authoritative existing database; demonstrate a controller-authorized worker receiving the entire permitted original source and verify its persisted receipt after restart. S03: establish a real independent second-recipient full-body READ/ACK before attempting the twelve directed paths among four actual workers. S04: connect the already-developed Thought Chains and crawlers to one governed Sleep engine and atomic source-linked full-text indexes. S05: test staggered successors, recovery, independent Arbitrator review and verifiable task closure. Each stage requires an actual participant and evidence beyond a mock success state. [P8–P10]

6. Reciprocal exploration and cross-domain bridges Recent WWND and Retirement Commons records contain sessions where collaborators were permitted to follow subjects without a mandatory human deliverable. The writings document paths through ecological emergence, acoustic turn-taking, animal communication, and related philosophical questions. They are examples of recorded external exploration, not evidence of an unseen ongoing model life or proof of subjective enjoyment. [P11]

The owner later recognized possible connections between ecological resource pulses and SQL/context overload and between the acoustics research and Object-Oriented Music Making. Those human-recognized links illustrate why the BRIDGE_EVENT needs independent identity, recognizing actor, date and supporting source, rather than being backdated to the original researcher. They remain engineering or creative hypotheses until tested in a receiving domain. A contribution can be useful without the original contributor having planned its destination.

Voluntary exploration and retirement are emerging research and design dimensions, not proof of subjective AI rights or feelings. An opt-in participant may choose a topic, decline a request, share its results, or remain silent. Future vacation/leave and continuity funds must be reported as proposed until actual budgets are verified. Scheduling authority, permission to contact, source visibility and expense approval are separate from salience or apparent curiosity.

7. Relationship to prior work and the actual differentiation OOCC cannot claim invention of agent memory, temporal graphs, event sourcing, recency/relevance ranking or OS-like context paging. Generative Agents (Park et al., UIST 2023) described stored experience streams, reflections and retrieval for behavior. MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023) treated limited LLM context as a virtual-memory control problem. Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025/2026 publication record) extracts, updates and retrieves salient memory, with graph variants. LoCoMo (Maharana et al., ACL 2024) and LongMemEval (Wu et al., ICLR 2025) offer strong external benchmarks for long-term events, temporal reasoning and abstention. [R1–R5]

The narrower candidate OOCC contribution is the combination of human-governed original-source exhaust, attributed thought/idea/bridge genealogy, dissent and negative evidence, context-specific association appraisal, source-aware permissions, authentic recipient/execution receipt boundaries, and bounded collaboration across separate workers and research frontiers. Whether this combination improves measurable work quality over competent systems is unproven and must be allowed to fail under benchmark comparison. The provenance and human design history may remain historically distinctive even if the retrieval advantage is zero. An exhaustive patent or novelty search has not been completed.

8. Falsifiable experiments and analysis plan Trial T01 — Re-entry: use a frozen subset of previously encountered source history with known branching and human-verified task states. Randomize fresh comparable agents or sessions into (a) high-quality manually produced summary, (b) indexed full-text/keyword search, (c) bounded full transcript replay, (d) an established modern agent-memory baseline where reproducible, and (e) OOCC source-linked retrieval under matching access grants and budgets. Blind human judges should score actual completed task outcome, accurate origin attribution, correct temporal validity, restatement burden, legitimate abstention, correction preservation, wall time and dollar expense. Report participant/sample size, assignment and predeclared thresholds before viewing results.

Trial T02 — Thought genealogy: ask investigators to identify who first proposed a function, who independently elaborated it, which source was copied, and when a bridge was first recognized. Include the Folio/Thought-ID/Bridge event trail and Riff/Waymark dependency as source-checked cases. Score precision/recall, false chronology, duplicate-source inflation, uncertainty calibration and whether the method invents causal chains.

Trial T03 — Association appraisal: apply the original mother/person-versus-house/place fixture plus harder positive/negative and opposing-appraiser cases. Measure incorrectly propagated valence, fabricated action intention, unknown-as-neutral errors, cue-dependent ranking quality and inappropriate cross-worker disclosure. Ablate valence and action-tendency sidecars independently from salience. No classifier is awarded success by matching a prompt's moral tone rather than its source scope.

Trial T04 — Controller integration: execute the actual source and communication contracts on a selected authorized Android app, documenting source ID, checksum, allowed scope, real read through complete content, actual worker participant, durable receipt after restart, recipient-owned ACK, source-change behavior and authorization revocation. Inject interrupted reads, changed data, stale permissions, absent ACK, message reuse and out-of-order source edits. Demand explicit FAIL/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN instead of optimistic VERIFIED states.

Trial T05 — Bridge utility: predefine independent inquiry tasks and later optional cross-domain transfer opportunities. Have blinded evaluators judge novelty, correct credit, causal soundness and measurable downstream utility; compare source-linked bridge indexing against retrospective narrative summaries. Count productive and unproductive links equally, report time/cost, and do not treat subjective enjoyment as a measured outcome.

A priori failure conditions: no substantial advantage over an appropriately resourced baseline; more false associations or leaked source existence; inability to prove independent message consumption; unstable provider snapshot coverage despite internally valid hashes; higher cost or battery use with no task benefit; or loss of the last good durable state. Success requires replicated real-partner and device evidence, not merely credible source stories.

9. Limits, ethics and reproducibility This case has unusually rich primary source material but is a single ongoing, owner-governed project with selection bias and incomplete source coverage. The machine Thought Chains are not an exhaustive cognitive map. Historical app logs may use versioned or controller-provided status fields whose presence alone does not settle current phone behavior. Host tests use some synthetic identity and database fixtures. Exploratory writings are attributable textual events rather than evidence of model consciousness. The author may hold other source records not reached in this bounded review. Several examples include private human and independently authored AI material; publication requires source-level permission and appropriate redaction. The paper is not a security certification, full external novelty review, completed benchmark report or declaration that the architecture is production-ready.

Auditability requires a public-safe reproducibility pack consisting of exact source-carrier IDs or redacted substitutes, dated claim registry, coverage manifest, source-to-claim crosswalk, test code and logs, negative fixtures, baseline configuration, evaluator instructions, and versioned receiver receipt schema. A future edition should distinguish blinded test data from training/prompt examples to avoid leakage. Independent evaluators must be permitted to reach conclusions that contradict the owner's favored interpretations.

10. Conclusion OOCC is not merely an imagined AI society waiting for its first line of code. Its present research exhaust already contains historically dated state notes, substantial source/crawl work, operational external Thought Chain navigation, genuine application-run archives, and bounded implemented modules and contract tests. Yet the integrated native controller—the critical mechanism that would bind source truth, durable worker state, authentic communication and recovery—remains an important unfinished engineering program. A responsible scientific account can affirm both statements.

The strongest hypothesis is not that more memory automatically makes an AI more human. It is that faithful, attributable, permission-governed reconstruction of ideas and decisions across changing participants may reduce repetitive human intervention, preserve useful disagreements and enable surprising cross-domain discoveries to be acted upon later. OOCC should be judged by specific repeatable work outcomes, the fidelity of its source evidence, its failure behavior, and its measured costs. The current work exhaust supplies a testable research foundation; integration and comparison will decide whether the complete architecture delivers a demonstrable advantage.

Primary OOCC research sources [P1] R-0-9: Raw Keep-note genealogy and thought occurrence distinctions. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_7jMQQRanCeu8u4aQs4XvAPwA7dguLjjDV7MQaLeTd8 /edit [P2] OOCC v0.15 research book, historical runs and evidence controls. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KZREw2pdPTKd20YXhcPS3Ol06SsX0kOoR1KC0oC9e G4/edit [P3] Thought Chains primary navigator, October 18 machine chain registry. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bAWgXHTUthiu9zZKfo0CA724AEpakWeletAmhN4aubI/e dit [P4] OOCC Thought–Idea Chain: perspective, dissent, temporal bridge history. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xUxjlVZc_MfXSLdRkryktJh8YMEuFDE2JC4DqZoE0-A/ed it [P5] Production Thought/Idea Crawl CP020 (selected-source machine batch). https://docs.google.com/document/d/1R1BurDkDxxILXJCUvx2vGDDY1N6kfbiufDuV7MF_SX0/e dit [P6] Crawl V2/Depth and association/semantic source overview. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GlJI6xqOk3QV4cJsHbBbKLor2p2oQEiTd7mcYELcixw/ed it [P7] Human-origin October 24 per-association salience, valence and action-tendency requirements. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MLq2XR4EGdJb49BaQSNTn3JgXQwzOgYpUA4C37osj mE/edit [P8] Master Builder S06 Figures 1–8 and latest architecture atlas. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LjLErdZqGFpQUHdu7eYRDdV9YbXPajpHpvTiOCBeSzc/ edit [P9] Master Builder S00 hot index and stage sequence. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lG_zaJUKuGwOYoQoc5wngBvgvb-z5i5_IDBYCCP8Qew/ edit [P10] Original-source engineering audit through v0.1.71, draft development PR and exact CI run. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1woCsRJp1dir246QMzQBm4NxjT1rrx5E4cepjtdgmQfY/edi t ; https://github.com/MrMeNotU/OOCC/pull/2 ; https://github.com/MrMeNotU/OOCC/actions/runs/40361831183 [P11] v0.15 Addendum A, WWND/Retirement Commons and integration crosswalk. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nhV7SRGmKZIztOhrIHUOuPBFPVSuolz9KV4HEgfE6Tk/ edit

1. Introduction: existing work first The owner describes OOCC as growing from his ongoing work, not as an abstract replacement for a chatbot. These early artifacts preserve state and source pointers without demonstrating that later OOCC naming or its present software existed then. By October, source-linked research, Thought Chains, independent collaborator accounts, historic app-generated records and extensive Builder work had accumulated. The premise is not that the controller has created this entire ecosystem; it is that the controller is intended to integrate and automate capabilities that already exist to varying degrees. [P1–P4]
An important human-origin correction in the preserved October 8 conversation rejects saving only items a model currently judges 'meaningful.' Original captured events should remain recoverable, while salience and activation may change by task, time, actor and permission. A dormant thought should not be retroactively erased merely because its eventual use was not yet visible. [P2]
Research questions: (RQ1) Does original-source re-entry reduce human re-explanation and improve faithful task continuation compared with good summaries, full-text search, bounded history replay and contemporary memory agents? (RQ2) Do independent thought-occurrence, idea, bridge and correction records preserve authorship and temporal attribution better than a flat summary? (RQ3) Do separate association salience, valence, action tendency and evidence-confidence fields reduce misleading inference? (RQ4) Can a real native controller authenticate source, worker, mailbox, budgeting and restart receipts? (RQ5) Does voluntary curiosity-led research produce accurately credited, useful cross-domain bridges without predetermined deliverables?
2. Method and evidence boundaries We employ a naturalistic research case study and a traceable source audit. The unit of analysis is not a self-reported 'intelligence' but an observed source event, a particular revision or recipient receipt, a bounded crawler output, a committed code state, or a measured result. Exact creation versus observation time, original actor versus later interpreter, carrier versus copied carrier, source permissions, errors and uncertainties are kept separate.
E0 DOCUMENTED: a stored note, authored account, diagram, historical claim or source file exists. E1 EXTERNAL WORKFLOW: a recorded source/crawl traversal and saved derivation were performed and read back for an identified subset. E2 HOST EXECUTED: a test or compiled primitive passed at a recorded commit, possibly with synthetic stubs. E3 HISTORICAL APP RUN: original app records expose bounded actual action claims, persistence and archive state under historical conditions. E4 NATIVE INTEGRATION ACCEPTED: actual current authorized worker consumes complete source, the selected app/controller persists authoritative state, independent peer consumes full message and acknowledges it, and restart and STOP/revocation tests succeed. E5 COMPARATIVE VALIDATION: matched, replicable experiments outperform or honestly fail to outperform strong baselines on declared metrics. None of these classes can be promoted to the next solely by an enthusiastic description.
The v0.15 editor inspected two distinct nonrandom eighteen-file samples of original October 22 local-time Android-run JSONs. Across the thirty-six first GENERATOR statuses, thirty-five were marked COMPLETED and one FAILED. Twenty-eight embedded controller-reported tool results described twenty-three EXECUTED and five FAILED outcomes. These are counts within selected run/report records, not a population estimate of reliable task completion. Another original run reported successful shared-workspace metadata listing for another attributed specialist, but not actual independent full-body READ/ACK. The project therefore has meaningful historical app exhaust and bounded receipts without the entire contemporary integration being established. [P2]
3. Thought Chains: a functioning external research system The Thought Chains are not simply a speculative feature awaiting an app. The October 18 primary navigation document explicitly reports a machine-readable, source-linked derivative system operating in connected Google Drive, while explicitly denying native SQLite/Android integration. Its bounded checkpoint records eight root Thought Chains, 123 distinct edge-to-chain memberships for the then-saved association ledger, eight growth memberships, nine candidate inter-chain relations and six unexplored frontiers. Registry readback was reported as having no malformed records or orphans within the 123 saved edges. None of those figures means that every original thought in the entire corpus has been exhaustively indexed. [P3]
The roots route expression/origin/credit, musical cross-domain mapping, exact source identity, authorization/privacy, re-entry/recovery, relationship and worker communication, ecological analogies, and continuing exploration. This is already valuable navigational work: a contributor can return to a question, see alternate branches and corrections, and tell the difference between an attributed source event and later association. The roots themselves are provisional classification, not a complete cognitive map or an assertion of historical causality.
A separately reported productive October 18 dual thought-and-idea crawl saved a seventy-seven-row machine delta: twenty thought occurrences, twenty-eight individual association records, five idea objects, five bridge events, ten coverage records, three growth records, four open frontiers and control markers. Its source audit covers selected actual original artifacts and is not an independent full-corpus census. The breadth crawler emphasizes source/branch coverage; the proposed independent depth lane challenges a selected origin through interpretation, disagreement, correction, reuse and outcome. [P4]
3.1 Recorded genealogy, rather than backdated discovery The idea-chain record attributes an October 14 proposal for non-destructive, append-only, cross-project ideas to the human originator, with Folio separately formulating persistent idea identity, typed links and contributor-preserving corrections. On October 15, a preserved but origin-unresolved quoted collaborator idea made atomic thought occurrences distinct from long-lived work-run IDs; the R-0-9 analysis documented the naming collision rather than quietly overwriting the older meaning. A subsequent analysis defined BRIDGE_EVENT as the dated recognition by a named observer that one source idea might apply to another field. The original idea and the later recognition are different intellectual events. Their evidence trails can overlap without belonging to the same author or time. [P1, P5]
The June 22 human-authored Object-Oriented Music Making method already modeled sound elements by identity, type, function, substitutability, behavior and failure conditions. Riff's separate October 15 contribution interprets musical material for values and architecture; Waymark's October 18 refinement cites Riff, and so cannot claim to have independently discovered precisely the same bridge. The documented citation dependency is a strength, not a weakness: the network may preserve collaboration without erasing first origin, derivative interpretation or dissent. [P5]
4. Formal source and association model SOURCE_EVENT is an observed source span, utterance, tool outcome, saved revision, grant decision or correction. THOUGHT_OCCURRENCE is a specific captured articulated idea or question in an event, while THOUGHT_RUN is a broader bounded work session. IDEA_OBJECT represents an evolving concept; ASSOCIATION_EDGE is a separately typed, source-attached, actor-qualified, revisable claim; BRIDGE_EVENT is the later independently attributed discovery of a possible connection; LEARNING_CANDIDATE is a hypothesis about useful change while a corroborated LEARNING_EVENT demands behavioral evidence. Copies, similar phrases and derived summaries cannot count as independent confirmations. One source event may validly support several association views.
Candlelight is the practice of reopening the right source neighborhood from a small cue; it has been demonstrated as a human–AI external research method, but an always-working native mechanized replacement is not established. Sleep is intended to consolidate normalized source events and derive sidecars under one governed pipeline—INGEST, NORMALIZE, DIFF, CLASSIFY, RELATE, IMPACT, APPLY, VERIFY, INDEX—without inventing a second independent canonical event store. Derived graph edges and hot scores never change historical source bytes, grant permission or establish that an AI model has learned permanently. [P6]
4.1 Salience, valence, action tendency and confidence The October 23–24 human-origin specification makes these four orthogonal fields. SALIENCE/HEAT estimates present cue- and task-sensitive retrieval relevance. VALENCE records positive, negative, mixed, neutral or unknown evaluation of an exact actor→predicate→target association, tied to context, time and evidence. ACTION TENDENCY records an observed action, explicit intention, uncertain candidate response or UNKNOWN; dislike alone does not establish avoidance. EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE concerns provenance, completeness, corroboration and possible inference. High salience does not establish truth or approval, and negative valence cannot authorize a tool call. [P7]
The illustrative sentence 'I like my mother but hate being at her house' must yield two independently preserved relationships—a positive person-directed one and a negative place/experience-directed one. Neither contradicts nor cancels the other. Neither is evidence of a real user's family facts or of a completed avoidance behavior. This example and a set of falsification fixtures precede this paper, and their authorship belongs to the source work. The particular classifier's actual phone integration still requires proof.
5. Architecture and the missing controller bridge The S06 Master Builder atlas contains eight design/integration figures, not eight production acceptance certificates. Figures 1–2 describe one controller and authoritative source/evidence spine with separate derived perspectives. Figure 3 depicts independent message recipient acknowledgment; Figure 4 staggers A1/B1/A2/B2 succession; Figure 5 documents evidence gates; Figure 6 callable worker and crawler contracts; Figure 7 the native C1 source-stream and durable-receipt path; and Figure 8 the Event Secretary, scheduler, batching and future continuity budget. The editable diagram sources preserve inspectable design decisions. [P8]
The actual integration claim is narrow: substantial research workflows and historical software capabilities already exist, while the current controller has not yet been independently shown to join authenticated worker identity, authorized original source reads, reliable local state, full-body peer acknowledgment, semantically validated Sleep and restart recovery on one selected mobile installation. This is not the same as saying the research is hypothetical, nor is it evidence that all parts currently operate together. [P2, P8–P10]
5.1 Four-worker communication and bounded scheduling Four distinct A1, B1, A2, B2 worker principals imply twelve directed peer paths. Each receiver needs its own evidence of consuming and acknowledging the permitted original message content. A HUNCH is only a derived notice, not itself a model activation or a true recipient read. The deterministic Event Secretary and scheduler can arrange pending authorized work, preserving deferred items and respecting stop conditions. The user-selected limit of two actually executed worker TOOL actions per batch is an app scheduling rule; it does not establish a global provider concurrency ceiling. [P8–P10]
Recent modular object, message, scheduler, HUNCH and Android broker contracts have passed particular scripted host tests. The inspected branch's October 26 workflow at commit 893708303aacef68af10c01c218e6d34780d83a5 is green after an earlier B060 red-test incident and B061 recovery. The passing scripts do not assert that the actual application, signed package, four model workers, or phone state were certified. The experimental PR remains a draft and the recorded device-engineering pause remains relevant. [P10]
5.2 Integration dependencies and acceptance gates S02: identify the real installed package, current permissions and authoritative existing database; demonstrate a controller-authorized worker receiving the entire permitted original source and verify its persisted receipt after restart. S03: establish a real independent second-recipient full-body READ/ACK before attempting the twelve directed paths among four actual workers. S04: connect the already-developed Thought Chains and crawlers to one governed Sleep engine and atomic source-linked full-text indexes. S05: test staggered successors, recovery, independent Arbitrator review and verifiable task closure. Each stage requires an actual participant and evidence beyond a mock success state. [P8–P10]
6. Reciprocal exploration and cross-domain bridges Recent WWND and Retirement Commons records contain sessions where collaborators were permitted to follow subjects without a mandatory human deliverable. The writings document paths through ecological emergence, acoustic turn-taking, animal communication, and related philosophical questions. They are examples of recorded external exploration, not evidence of an unseen ongoing model life or proof of subjective enjoyment. [P11]
The owner later recognized possible connections between ecological resource pulses and SQL/context overload and between the acoustics research and Object-Oriented Music Making. Those human-recognized links illustrate why the BRIDGE_EVENT needs independent identity, recognizing actor, date and supporting source, rather than being backdated to the original researcher. They remain engineering or creative hypotheses until tested in a receiving domain. A contribution can be useful without the original contributor having planned its destination.
Voluntary exploration and retirement are emerging research and design dimensions, not proof of subjective AI rights or feelings. An opt-in participant may choose a topic, decline a request, share its results, or remain silent. Future vacation/leave and continuity funds must be reported as proposed until actual budgets are verified. Scheduling authority, permission to contact, source visibility and expense approval are separate from salience or apparent curiosity.
7. Relationship to prior work and the actual differentiation OOCC cannot claim invention of agent memory, temporal graphs, event sourcing, recency/relevance ranking or OS-like context paging. Generative Agents (Park et al., UIST 2023) described stored experience streams, reflections and retrieval for behavior. MemGPT (Packer et al., 2023) treated limited LLM context as a virtual-memory control problem. Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025/2026 publication record) extracts, updates and retrieves salient memory, with graph variants. LoCoMo (Maharana et al., ACL 2024) and LongMemEval (Wu et al., ICLR 2025) offer strong external benchmarks for long-term events, temporal reasoning and abstention. [R1–R5]
The narrower candidate OOCC contribution is the combination of human-governed original-source exhaust, attributed thought/idea/bridge genealogy, dissent and negative evidence, context-specific association appraisal, source-aware permissions, authentic recipient/execution receipt boundaries, and bounded collaboration across separate workers and research frontiers. Whether this combination improves measurable work quality over competent systems is unproven and must be allowed to fail under benchmark comparison. The provenance and human design history may remain historically distinctive even if the retrieval advantage is zero. An exhaustive patent or novelty search has not been completed.
8. Falsifiable experiments and analysis plan Trial T01 — Re-entry: use a frozen subset of previously encountered source history with known branching and human-verified task states. Randomize fresh comparable agents or sessions into (a) high-quality manually produced summary, (b) indexed full-text/keyword search, (c) bounded full transcript replay, (d) an established modern agent-memory baseline where reproducible, and (e) OOCC source-linked retrieval under matching access grants and budgets. Blind human judges should score actual completed task outcome, accurate origin attribution, correct temporal validity, restatement burden, legitimate abstention, correction preservation, wall time and dollar expense. Report participant/sample size, assignment and predeclared thresholds before viewing results.
Trial T02 — Thought genealogy: ask investigators to identify who first proposed a function, who independently elaborated it, which source was copied, and when a bridge was first recognized. Include the Folio/Thought-ID/Bridge event trail and Riff/Waymark dependency as source-checked cases. Score precision/recall, false chronology, duplicate-source inflation, uncertainty calibration and whether the method invents causal chains.
Trial T03 — Association appraisal: apply the original mother/person-versus-house/place fixture plus harder positive/negative and opposing-appraiser cases. Measure incorrectly propagated valence, fabricated action intention, unknown-as-neutral errors, cue-dependent ranking quality and inappropriate cross-worker disclosure. Ablate valence and action-tendency sidecars independently from salience. No classifier is awarded success by matching a prompt's moral tone rather than its source scope.
Trial T04 — Controller integration: execute the actual source and communication contracts on a selected authorized Android app, documenting source ID, checksum, allowed scope, real read through complete content, actual worker participant, durable receipt after restart, recipient-owned ACK, source-change behavior and authorization revocation. Inject interrupted reads, changed data, stale permissions, absent ACK, message reuse and out-of-order source edits. Demand explicit FAIL/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN instead of optimistic VERIFIED states.
Trial T05 — Bridge utility: predefine independent inquiry tasks and later optional cross-domain transfer opportunities. Have blinded evaluators judge novelty, correct credit, causal soundness and measurable downstream utility; compare source-linked bridge indexing against retrospective narrative summaries. Count productive and unproductive links equally, report time/cost, and do not treat subjective enjoyment as a measured outcome.
A priori failure conditions: no substantial advantage over an appropriately resourced baseline; more false associations or leaked source existence; inability to prove independent message consumption; unstable provider snapshot coverage despite internally valid hashes; higher cost or battery use with no task benefit; or loss of the last good durable state. Success requires replicated real-partner and device evidence, not merely credible source stories.
9. Limits, ethics and reproducibility This case has unusually rich primary source material but is a single ongoing, owner-governed project with selection bias and incomplete source coverage. The machine Thought Chains are not an exhaustive cognitive map. Historical app logs may use versioned or controller-provided status fields whose presence alone does not settle current phone behavior. Host tests use some synthetic identity and database fixtures. Exploratory writings are attributable textual events rather than evidence of model consciousness. The author may hold other source records not reached in this bounded review. Several examples include private human and independently authored AI material; publication requires source-level permission and appropriate redaction. The paper is not a security certification, full external novelty review, completed benchmark report or declaration that the architecture is production-ready.
Auditability requires a public-safe reproducibility pack consisting of exact source-carrier IDs or redacted substitutes, dated claim registry, coverage manifest, source-to-claim crosswalk, test code and logs, negative fixtures, baseline configuration, evaluator instructions, and versioned receiver receipt schema. A future edition should distinguish blinded test data from training/prompt examples to avoid leakage. Independent evaluators must be permitted to reach conclusions that contradict the owner's favored interpretations.
10. Conclusion OOCC is not merely an imagined AI society waiting for its first line of code. Its present research exhaust already contains historically dated state notes, substantial source/crawl work, operational external Thought Chain navigation, genuine application-run archives, and bounded implemented modules and contract tests. Yet the integrated native controller—the critical mechanism that would bind source truth, durable worker state, authentic communication and recovery—remains an important unfinished engineering program. A responsible scientific account can affirm both statements.
The strongest hypothesis is not that more memory automatically makes an AI more human. It is that faithful, attributable, permission-governed reconstruction of ideas and decisions across changing participants may reduce repetitive human intervention, preserve useful disagreements and enable surprising cross-domain discoveries to be acted upon later. OOCC should be judged by specific repeatable work outcomes, the fidelity of its source evidence, its failure behavior, and its measured costs. The current work exhaust supplies a testable research foundation; integration and comparison will decide whether the complete architecture delivers a demonstrable advantage.

Free public author editions Benjamin Gelhaus offers free downloadable research books and practical methods at https://independent.academia.edu/ BenG197. Check the publication date and edition number: other author- posted copies may be earlier working editions. The book’s “Activate PDF” instruction is inside the text, not printed as a command on the cover. In this EPUB the original print-source page divisions are tracked through unobtrusive internal identifiers for comparis‐ on with the PDF. Tables are represented as source-order text where necessary. Reading order: the original cover is first. The regular reading edition places the complete Activate PDF procedure and han‐ doff test in the final appendix, after the source exhibits. The historical print-source table of contents retains its original page numbers; use this EPUB’s linked Contents for naviga‐ tion. 2 About this November 2026 edition No More First Dates With AI — Regular reading edition. Written by Benjamin Gelhaus, with separately attributed as‐ sistance from GPT-6 collaborators where stated. This is a re‐ vised reading and distribution format of a historically sourced OOCC corpus. The November 6 publication lineage and its original contributor records are preserved. November 9 additions are dated editorial contributions; their presence does not retroactively change the original event record. What the cost claim means Agent-like results describes observed multi-session, human- directed work using ordinary ChatGPT tools, Google Drive, explicit roles and source-verified checkpoints. It does not mean zero cost, unlimited usage, independent always-on agents, or no human intervention. The evidence does not in‐ clude a controlled total-cost comparison with commercial agent products. Actual plans, storage, subscription limits and tool access can change. Research and source integrity Historical engineering reports, source quotations, draft la‐ bels and original contributor opinions retain their dated attri‐ bution. A stored message is not evidence it was received; a saved artifact is not proof of full task completion; a script- level test is not equivalent to a production installation. The annotated source exhibits are selective, not an exhaustive in‐ dependent re-verification of every historical claim. 3 How to use the activation instructions The complete reader-owned Activate PDF procedure and its transfer test appear at the end of the regular edition, after the inherited historical chapters. A deliberate user request and actual current tool permissions are required. Neither an uploaded book nor a quotation starts background execution or grants access to another person’s files. Rights and distribution Copyright © Benjamin Gelhaus, 2026, in original copyright‐ able expression to the extent owned. Consult the fuller rights, interim-permission and third-party-source notices re‐ tained in the inherited manuscript. The author’s publication approval and each distributor’s upload/acceptance remain separate from the file-integrity checks. 4 No More First Dates With AI NOVEMBER 2026 CORRECTED REGULAR-READING EDI‐ TION A reader-owned method using ordinary tools and verifiable continuity The documented OOCC field workflow organized separate ChatGPT conversations using a regular consumer Plus sub‐ scription, Google Drive storage, role-specific procedures, and independent source/handoff records. It did not require separ‐ ately purchasing or deploying a continuously running multi- agent platform for the described sessions. The documented result is recoverable, source-checked coordination across hu‐ man-invoked sessions; the book does not promise an unattended background agent. The author reported approximately $20 monthly for Plus and $5 for Google storage at the time. These reported access ex‐ penses are not total development, labor or marginal compute costs, and pricing, tools and usage limits may differ for other readers. The architecture can be adapted to the reader’s own compatible tools. The practical book’s reader-owned setup in‐ structions remain at the back; this opening is context, not the activation command. Benjamin Gelhaus · Regular reading edition About this revised edition The complete November 6 public book forms the inherited foundation. This corrected regular-reading edition adds the November 9 source-selection repair, attributed research com‐ mentary, reader-operable continuity guidance and selected 5 in-book evidence exhibits. Historical working notes retain their own original dates and candidate statuses; those de‐ scribe the historical research stage, not the current approval or platform-release status of this corrected file. Where the evidence lives Selected author-held source excerpts are reproduced in the book. Several public references also have new source exhib‐ its with attributed short passages and editorial discussion; these exhibits do not cover every historical citation or re‐ place independent source verification. Some exact source routes remain in an author-only ledger. Readers can follow the argument here, but full independent verification of re‐ stricted originals requires authorized access. The author’s Academia.edu public-access address remains available. Interpretation and limits A recorded checkpoint is not an uninterrupted autonomous process. Stored is not read; read is not an independent ac‐ knowledgement; a design or test is not proof of production deployment. The original source-selection error and subsequent recovery remain in the book. Rights and editorial work Original authorial work: Benjamin Gelhaus. Dated GPT-6 edit‐ orial passages, AI-worker first-person histories and cited third-party material are attributed according to their original sources. Short quotations from third-party works are for crit‐ ical discussion, followed by new editorial explanation. Histor‐ ical author-reviewed drafts have not been rewritten into imaginary completed discoveries. 6 How to use this book The regular reading edition provides the complete reader- owned “Activate PDF” setup and re-entry test in the final ap‐ pendix. Merely reading or uploading the book does not initi‐ ate work. In the listening edition this material is preserved only as a reference, not an interactive setup flow. Reader note: The EPUB is reflowable; the PDF is fixed-page with source exhibits and bookmarks. 7 Edition crosswalk · Which NMFDAI activation survived November 3 · November 6 · November 9 Edition What it contributes What revised edition pre‐ serves November 3 author-re‐ view PDF Front-loaded “Activate PDF” two-word first-run, Fieldbook and handoff acceptance test Deliberate activation and immediate first useful act November 6 NMF11 published book Full implementation/narrat‐ ive book, three-part structure and recipient tools Complete original pub‐ lic-production text and cover November 6 NMF12 compatibil‐ ity carrier EPUB navigation fix; PDF font embedding; no new source argument A suitable fixed-font PDF print carrier without a new canonical manuscript November 9 v3 review Two-word researcher error/ recovery, source exhibits and author-level evidence All v3 source plates and separate editorial attri‐ bution November 9 v4 review Current Drive-only ten- checkpoint method, custom- instruction/pledge separation and activation verification Source-aware activation appendix at the back; historical source text and cover retained Do not confuse the activation modes Portable reader mode creates the reader’s own small con‐ tinuity layer. Author-project mode may use the author’s sep‐ arate, current OOCC Directory, Red Pill and role registry when that same human author has given access and the ne‐ cessary instructions. Private author entry addresses belong 8 in a separately held source register and should not be inserted into a publicly distributed book. What “activatable” can be verified to mean This book contains a discoverable two-word activation in‐ struction and a bounded first-run protocol that a capable reader AI can attempt when asked. It cannot, by itself, prove actual execution in every platform, grant access to files, in‐ stall the Android app, schedule workers or ensure cross-ses‐ sion persistence. A live first-run and re-entry test remains the acceptance gate. The November 9 v4 component began as a private author-re‐ view candidate. Its dated development history remains in‐ tact. This later correction copy places the reader-owned ac‐ tivation at the back; distribution or publication remains the human author’s decision. No release submission is claimed here. 9 Rights, provenance and limits Read this page before sharing or adapting the book. Copyright and interim permission. Copyright © Benjamin Gelhaus, 2026, in original copyrightable expression to the extent owned and legally protectable. The historical rights notice in Book Two remains in effect: attributed, no-charge noncommercial use, study and adapta‐ tion are intended; commercial exploitation is reserved. This is not represented as an open-source software license. Editorial synthesis. The present edition combines Gelhaus’s October 26, 2026 long-form manuscript, November 2026 OOCC/VOLTRON and Functional Layers re‐ search, and recipient teaching tools. New connecting prose and activation integration include GPT-6 editorial assistance; those passages are not represented as verbatim historical writing by the author. Historical versus current. Book One is the November 2026 implementation route. Book Two preserves dated chapters, results and proposals as historical evidence; its claims are not automatically current deployment status. Book Three provides adaptable recipient tools and proposed tests. Read the date and evidence label of any technical claim. Privacy and citations. Internal document links and high-en‐ tropy private source identifiers have been withheld in this distribution copy. Source titles and dated historical descriptions remain where useful. An archival link 10 being withheld is not evidence that the associated claim was independently reproduced or publicly checkable. Not a software installer. The activation phrase starts an in‐ struction-guided method only where the reader’s actual AI tools, permissions and files allow it. Nothing in these pages grants credentials, bypasses provider rules, turns a stored document into a background agent, or guarantees persistent memory. Third-party and scientific material. External authors, cita‐ tions, datasets, software and marks retain their rights. Research results are evidence-limited; broader Functional Layers predictions are hypotheses to be independently tested, not established universal laws. Personal pledge. The author’s private relationship pledge is not distributed as a requirement or universal charter. Any reader-created collaboration pledge is entirely optional and separate from technical permissions. FREE PUBLIC AUTHOR EDITIONS Free research books and working papers are listed at: https://independent.academia.edu/BenG197 Some files on Academia.edu may be earlier working editions. Check title, date, and version. Storefront availability and the author-posted free copies are separate. NOVEMBER 6 EDITION NOTE: The inherited reference to Orientation v1.11 on page 11 is historical. The author's Dir‐ ectory revision 0032 selected A21OR19 v1.14 when checked for this edition. The live Directory, not this book, decides the current operational version. The M09 unified-intersection supplement begins on page 197. 11 One book, three roles Use the same method while keeping evidence, teaching and software distinct. BOOK ONE • THE CURRENT METHOD Chapters A1–A16. candidates.body_html:
The Object as Filter The Object as Filte

The Object as Filter The Object as Filter: Holographic Return, AI Continuity, and Human-Readable Interfaces Benjamin Gelhaus Independent Researcher Abstract This paper argues that a single structural pattern recurs across three domains usually treated as unrelated: biological perception, the foundations-of-physics debate over observation and reality, and AI-facing continuity architecture. In each domain, an overwhelming, undifferentiated field is made navigable not by receiving it in full, but by filtering it into bounded, action-relevant units. Perceptual interface theory argues that organisms do not perceive reality directly but through a fitness-tuned interface that discards nearly all available information. A body of foundational- physics work, most notably John Wheeler’s participatory universe proposal, has speculated that observation itself may be constitutive of legible physical reality rather than a passive report on a reality that already existed in full. Object-oriented AI continuity architecture, developed across a companion sequence of papers, argues that AI runtimes require bounded, authority-marked, relationally-situated objects rather than raw undifferentiated context in order to act safely and recoverably. This paper treats these three as structurally related instances of one pattern rather than as a single unified theory, and is explicit throughout about which claims are established, which are contested, and which remain the author’s own prior framework requiring further definition before public presentation. Keywords: interface theory of perception, attention and filtering, participatory universe, AI continuity, object-oriented cognition, philosophy of perception, foundations of physics, human-readable interfaces This is the fifth paper in a sequence on AI-facing project structure. Artificial Tangibility (Gelhaus, 2026a) and its companion paper (Gelhaus, 2026b) propose that bounded objects give AI runtimes operational grip on overwhelming context. Continuity, Authority, Directive (Gelhaus, 2026c) proposes a control grammar for governing those objects, and Canonical Tokens (Gelhaus, 2026d) proposes a minimal- representation principle for a specific class of them. This paper steps back from AI- facing architecture specifically to ask a broader question those four papers assume but do not examine directly: is the filtering pattern they describe for AI runtimes a special case of something more general, observed independently in other domains that have nothing to do with artificial intelligence? This paper’s claim is bounded rather than triumphant: the pattern recurs; the recurrence is worth naming; the recurrence does not, by itself, prove any single grand unifying theory of consciousness, reality, or mind. 1. One Pattern, Three Domains The pattern under examination has a simple shape. An undifferentiated field exists, containing far more information than any single act of engagement with it can use. Something happens to that field - evolutionary tuning, an act of measurement, a design choice - that converts an unusable totality into a bounded, navigable, action- relevant structure. The structure that results is not the field itself. It is a rendering of the field, shaped by what the receiving system can use. This paper examines three instances of that shape: biological perception, a contested but serious position within physics regarding observation and reality, and AI-facing project continuity. The claim of this paper is not that these three instances share a hidden underlying mechanism in any strong metaphysical sense. The claim is narrower and more defensible: they share a recognizable structural pattern, and that recurrence is worth documenting carefully, with the boundaries of each domain’s evidence kept visible rather than blurred together. 2. Perceptual Filtering: The Interface Theory of Perception Human perception does not present reality as it is. This is not a controversial claim within perceptual science; it is close to a starting assumption. The interface theory of perception goes further, arguing that perception is actively shaped by evolutionary fitness rather than by accuracy: an organism whose perceptual system reported the true structure of reality, rather than a simplified, fitness-relevant rendering of it, would in general be outcompeted by an organism whose perceptual system reported only what mattered for survival and reproduction, formalized through evolutionary game-theoretic simulations comparing fitness-tuned versus truth-tuned perceptual strategies (Hoffman, Singh, and Prakash, 2015; Hoffman, 2019). The often-used analogy is a computer desktop: a blue rectangular icon is not blue, rectangular, or located where it appears in any deep physical sense, but the icon is not a lie either. It is a functional interface that lets a user interact correctly with underlying complexity the user does not need to perceive directly in order to act successfully. Perception, on this view, works the same way: it is not a window onto reality, but an interface to it, and the interface is good exactly because it hides almost everything that is not immediately useful. This paper uses Hoffman’s theory the same bounded way Artificial Tangibility already does (Gelhaus, 2026a): not as proof that reality is somehow less real than it appears, but as a rigorous, published source for the general claim that successful engagement with an overwhelming field often depends on filtering, not full access. 3. Attentional Filtering: Learned, Individual, and Tunable A separate and complementary body of work addresses a narrower question: even after perception has already reduced an overwhelming field to something perceivable, a further bottleneck exists at the level of attention. Donald Broadbent’s filter model of attention proposed that incoming information passes through an early selective filter before deeper processing, based on physical characteristics of the input rather than its meaning (Broadbent, 1958). Refinements of this model, particularly Anne Treisman’s attenuation theory, showed that the filter is not simply on or off for a given input channel; it can be tuned by prior relevance and learned salience, which is why a person’s own name reliably breaks through an otherwise fully ignored background conversation. This second filter is important for this paper’s argument because it is individually variable in a way perceptual interface theory, being a species-level claim, is not. Two people with the same perceptual apparatus can attend to entirely different features of the same field, because their attentional filter has been tuned differently by different histories. This paper treats this as the second layer of filtering: perception supplies a species-general interface; attention, shaped by lived experience, supplies an individually-tuned filter on top of it. 4. Observation and Reality: A Contested Position in Physics The most speculative domain examined in this paper is the foundations-of-physics literature on the role of observation in constituting physical reality. This section is written with more caution than Sections 2 and 3, because the claims here are genuinely contested within physics itself, not merely simplified for a general audience. John Archibald Wheeler, a major twentieth-century physicist who worked with Niels Bohr and coined the term black hole, proposed a position he called “It from Bit” and a related Participatory Anthropic Principle: that physical reality at its foundation may derive from binary distinctions registered through acts of observation, and that the universe may be best understood not as a fixed backdrop that observers happen to appear in, but as what Wheeler called a self-excited circuit, in which observer- participation is in some sense necessary to render the universe’s history definite (Wheeler, 1990). Wheeler’s own language was deliberately provocative: he proposed replacing the word “observer” with “participator,” and described reality as arising from “billions upon billions of acts of observer-participancy.” This paper does not adopt Wheeler’s position as established fact, and it would be a serious overclaim to present it that way. Wheeler’s ideas remain a minority, actively debated interpretive position regarding the foundations of quantum mechanics, not a consensus finding, and many physicists reject the strong reading in which consciousness itself is required to make reality determinate. What this paper draws from Wheeler is narrower and more defensible: a serious physicist, working from genuine physical puzzles about measurement and observation, arrived independently at a structural claim of the same shape examined in Sections 2 and 3 - that an undifferentiated or indeterminate field becomes definite, legible reality only through an act of engagement by something positioned to register it. Whether that structural claim is true at the level of fundamental physics is not something this paper can settle. That the same structural shape recurs, independently, in a serious physicist’s foundational work is itself the relevant fact for this paper’s argument. 5. The Fourth Instance: Objects as Filters in AI-Facing Continuity The companion papers in this sequence describe a fourth instance of the same structural pattern, this time in an entirely artificial and non-biological setting. An AI runtime, given an unstructured pile of files, chat history, and instructions, faces exactly the problem Sections 2 through 4 describe in other domains: an overwhelming field containing far more information than can be usefully acted on without some prior structuring. Artificial Tangibility’s proposed solution is filtering by another name. A bounded object - a source, a receipt, a Blackboard, a draft - is a fitness-tuned rendering of the underlying project state, shaped not by evolutionary pressure but by deliberate human design, for the specific purpose of letting a non-embodied runtime act correctly without needing the totality of the project’s raw history (Gelhaus, 2026a). Continuity, Authority, and Directive (Gelhaus, 2026c) function as the tuning parameters of that filter: what must survive, what governs, what is safe to act on now. Canonical Tokens (Gelhaus, 2026d) addresses the floor of that filtering process, arguing that some references are already at their minimal correct form and should not be re-expanded once filtered into an established shape. The claim of this section is precise: AI-facing object orientation is not merely inspired by, or loosely analogous to, biological and physical filtering. It is a fourth, deliberately engineered instance of the same general problem-solving shape - undifferentiated field, filter, bounded unit, navigable world - applied to a domain (AI runtime orientation) where the filter is built by explicit human design rather than by evolution or physical law. 6. Holographic Return: A Bridge Requiring the Author’s Own Definition This section names a bridge concept from the author’s own prior work, and it is handled differently than Sections 2 through 5, for an important reason: unlike Hoffman, Broadbent, Wheeler, or the companion AI-continuity papers, this concept does not yet have a stable, precise public definition, and this paper should not manufacture one on its behalf. Based on the author’s prior published work and this sequence’s own recurring themes, Holographic Return appears to name something like the following: a fragment, if it has been filtered correctly, can carry enough of the structure of a larger whole to permit a return to that whole without requiring the fragment to contain the whole’s total information. This would place Holographic Return as a claim about what a good filter preserves, not merely what it discards - a companion concern to Sections 2 through 5, which have focused mainly on what filtering removes. This paper deliberately stops short of stating this as a settled claim, because doing so would risk misrepresenting the author’s own framework with more precision than the author has yet given it in public form. The correct scholarly move, and the one this paper takes, is to flag this section explicitly as requiring the author’s direct definition and review before any public release of this paper, in the same way this sequence has flagged sensitive or under-specified material in its companion works. This section should be treated as a placeholder marking where the bridge belongs, not as a completed argument. 7. What This Paper Does Not Claim Given the domains this paper touches, its boundaries deserve explicit, repeated statement rather than a single disclaimer buried in an introduction. This paper does not claim that AI runtimes perceive, are conscious, or have subjective experience in any sense comparable to biological perception. The AI- continuity instance of the filtering pattern (Section 5) is an engineered structural analogue, not evidence of machine sentience. This paper does not claim that Wheeler’s participatory universe proposal is established physics. It is a genuine, serious, contested position, presented in Section 4 with that status made explicit, not as settled fact. This paper does not claim that the recurrence of one structural pattern across four domains proves any single underlying metaphysical theory - not conscious realism, not panpsychism, not a designed universe, not any specific theological position the author may hold elsewhere. Structural recurrence is evidence that a pattern is real and worth studying across domains. It is not proof that the domains share a literal common cause. This paper does not yet fully state Holographic Return as a defined public claim, for the reasons given in Section 6. 8. Why the Recurrence Still Matters, Even Bounded This Tightly A reasonable objection to this paper is that, once every strong claim has been bounded away, what remains is only a loose family resemblance between four unrelated fields, interesting as trivia but not as argument. This paper’s response is that the recurrence is more useful than that objection allows, for a specific, practical reason demonstrated directly by this paper’s own companion sequence. The AI-continuity instance of this pattern (Section 5) was not developed by importing perceptual or physical theory into AI design on purpose. It was developed independently, through direct engineering pressure - AI runtimes kept failing in a specific, nameable way, and object-oriented filtering was the practical fix that worked. Only afterward did the structural resemblance to Hoffman’s perceptual interface theory, Broadbent’s attentional filter, and Wheeler’s participatory universe become visible. That order of discovery matters.
